price_why: A tier-one idea (three hackle densities, same setup, bare-count hook) is specific enough to shoot tonight. Three more concepts with covers and hooks, plus the herbarium-card and knolled-recipe framings, would save a fly tyer several ideation sessions. Some of the paper is research-process noise and 'no saves seen' filler, so I wouldn't go higher.
one_line: A heavily researched content brief that gives one fully specified, on-niche 'make this first' carousel, a few cross-niche formats adapted to fly tying, and a good deal of research-process padding.
strongest: The 'Three hackles' carousel: three identical Partridge & Orange flies differing only in hackle turns, same camera and light, a bare-count hook, and a stated way it can fail. It suits beginner tyers, needs only what's on the table, and comes with a clear reason to make it first.
weakest: Much of the length is other-niche scaffolding, source bookkeeping, and sections that don't help the next post: repeated empty 'Taste: no saves seen' lines, a thin 'What is moving' list that is mostly foam and salmon patterns, and a forum view-count aside. Several secondary ideas (Problem→Cause→Fix, one-year comparison, specimen card) lack a settled hook or format.
